messages.subject: Incorporating specific quadrature weights
parts:
Hi Phil,

I was wondering what the correct way to incorporate specific quadrature weights would be. Suppose I have:

mirt_data is a data.frame of item-response data that I'm going to fit to the 3PL model. Also:

qval <- seq(-4, 4, by = .2) # 41 quadrature points evenly spaced
qwgh <- c(.000027,.000058,.000122,.000246,.000477,.000886,.001583,.002717,.004479,.007095,.010799,.015791,.022185,.029947,.038839,      .048396,.057941,.066648,.073657,.078212,.079792,.078212,.073657,.066648,.057941,.048396,.038839,.029947,.022185,.015791,      .010799,.007095,.004479,.002717,.001583,.000886,.000477,.000246,.000122,.000058,.000027)

I think that I can incorporate the quadrature points this way:

mirt(data = mirt_data, model = 1, itemtype = '3PL', quadpts = 41, technical = list(theta_lim = c(-4,4), customTheta = matrix(qval,ncol=1)))

But I'm not sure how to specify the weights in qwgh. Can you please help?

By the way, if I specify customTheta, do I also need to specify quadpts = 41 as I did above or is that redundant since customTheta is already a 41x1 matrix in this case?

Best,
Jon
